document_title: Austin Community College is writing its AI policy
_note: Slide strings read off the render report's text nodes and each frame's own source line by build_copy.py.
caption:
Austin Community College calls its coming AI policy its "first-ever."

Its October 9th post says a framework called TRUST is meant to help shape it. The third rule reads "AI can support your work, but it should never replace your expertise, decision-making, or responsibility." The college says more than 79,000 students rely on it each year.

The Faculty and Student AI Town Hall on October 12th at the Rio Grande Campus will explore in-progress AI policies. The October 22nd seminar at the Highland Campus is open to community members.

The college's AI Resource Hub already links a faculty and staff document titled Acceptable Use of Artificial Intelligence Policy.

The post names no adoption date, no vote and no adopting body. Who decides whether the new policy replaces that document or sits beside it?

#AustinCommunityCollege #AustinTX #TRUSTFramework

S5.headline: The judgment stays with the person
S5.body: "AI can support your work, but it should never replace your expertise, decision-making, or responsibility," the third rule reads. The first asks people to say when AI plays a meaningful role.

S6.headline: Three dates on fourteen pavers
S6.body: One paver for each day from the October 9th post to the October 22nd seminar at Highland, both ends counted. The town hall is October 12th at Rio Grande. A faculty convocation titled The Two AIs is October 16th at Eastview.

S7.headline: The walk ends where the post does
S7.body: The post names no adoption date, no vote and no adopting body. Its last date is the October 22nd seminar. It is a guided discussion of E. M. Forster's story The Machine Stops.

S8.body: The college says its Faculty and Student AI Town Hall will explore in-progress AI policies. It runs until 9 p.m. at the Rio Grande Campus. The room is drawn to illustrate.

S9.headline: Community members are invited too
S9.body: The college invites faculty, staff, students and community members to take part in one or more of the events. Feedback and questions go through a form on its page about getting involved with generative AI.
